direction-type.words: Dominant seventh chord on the second scale degree (secondary dominant)
and diminished seventh chord on the raised second scale degree
These chords may appear due to passing chromatic tones.
Most often they are used in the first and second inversion in cadences.
(here the six-four chord cannot be skipped)
Also, these chords can be used after the triads of the first or sixth or fourth scale degree.
In a minor, the secondary dominant, in addition
to raising the third, also requires raising the fifth.
In the second inversion, this is not very common.
In a minor, a diminished seventh chord is not possible
on the second scale degree, but can be formed on the
fourth scale degree by raising the root and third.
